O Sakhi Gopal! You have kept the pledge of Your servant, the Brahmin. ||4||6||56|| ☬ His story is this: from a village called Khurdanapur, five kos this side of Jagannath ji, two Brahmins — one of high caste and one of low caste — went together on pilgrimage. At Brindaban the elder fell ill, and the other served him devotedly. When he recovered, he promised him his daughter's hand in marriage; but back in the village, misled by his relatives, he went back on his word. A dispute arose, and the court asked for a witness. He said, "My Gopal is my witness." The court said, "If He comes and bears witness, your match stands." That Brahmin went and sat in vigil until he brought Him along. Gopal bore witness and helped His servant. The story is well known in the Bhagatmal. ☬ He speaks of the greatness of Sri Amritsar ji, or of the true company:
